Kimberly / team — reviewed Horizon's redline and procurement ask. Below are practical options we can propose (legal language draft attached):

Option A (Sales-friendly):
- Accept 30-day auto-renew notice.
- Add explicit offboarding assistance: Redwood will provide 30 days of transition support (standard T&M) and reasonable assistance to export data.
- No refunds for prepaid tokens, but we can offer pro-rated credits for unused committed capacity during the remaining billing period if the customer halts usage in writing.

Option B (Risk-balanced, recommended):
- Compromise to a 45-day auto-renew notice (gives ops runway).
- Include a 60-day termination-for-convenience wind-down commitment with limited credits: refund of any unused prepaid committed capacity pro-rated over remaining term, plus up to 30 days of prioritized transition assistance at no charge.
- Add a mutual termination clause (either party) so both sides have symmetry.

Contract language notes (attached doc): we recommend: (i) an explicit definition of "Notice Period" in the Term section, (ii) a short paragraph in Termination for Convenience describing wind-down assistance and refund mechanics, and (iii) a cap on cumulative refunds equal to the unused committed fees to avoid open-ended liability.

Operational impact: 30 days creates real scheduling risk for GPU reservations; 45 days is a pragmatic middle ground. If Sales is willing to provide a one-time onboarding/transition credit (or a small revenue commitment), we can accept 45 days with the wind-down protections above.

Happy to refine language — I attached the draft redline.

-Karthik
